newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fin mins urge Belgium to further trim deficit.
newsitem.headline: EU fin mins urge Belgium to further trim deficit.

text.p: European Union finance ministers urged Belgium on Monday to trim its deficit to 2.3 percent of gross domestic product in 1998 from the planned 2.9 percent in 1997.

"Such a step is necessary to secure a durable budgetary adjustment, to lessen the vulnerability of public finances to cyclical fluctuations and to hasten the continued reduction in the debt ratio," the EU ministers said in a review of Belgium's 1996 budgetary situation.

The finance ministers noted Belgium's debt at the end of 1996 at 130.0 percent of GDP was "considerably above" the 60 percent reference target set in the Maastricht Treaty on economic and monetary union (EMU).
They also noted the 2.3 percent target was already laid down in Belgium's three-year, forward economic plan published, alongside the 1997 budget, in October 1996.
That "convergence plan" was given a thumbs up by the finance ministers at a separate meeting in January.
Monday's review formed part of the EU's annual examination of which member states ran "excessive budget deficits" in the previous year.
Under the Maastricht Treaty, countries participating in EMU must have been judged not to be running excessive deficits.
As expected, Monday's gathering of finance ministers agreed to add Finland and the Netherlands to the list of countries -- Ireland, Denmark and Luxembourg -- already deemed to have passed the test.
A decision on the UK was postponed pending the new Labour government's planned budget in June.

Next year's excessive deficits examination will take place alongside the decision on which EU members qualify to take part in EMU from 1999. That decision is due to be made at the end of April or beginning of May 1998.
